post.caption:
A voice cannot travel as radio on its own, so it rides on a carrier wave. AM varies the carrier's size in the shape of the voice, FM squeezes and stretches it instead, and the receiver strips the carrier away at the far end. Different bands behave differently: long waves bend around obstacles, short ones need line of sight, and at night the ionosphere bounces AM back down so it carries much further. Bandwidth is genuinely finite, which is why spectrum is auctioned like land.
